fulltext: IT之家 10 月 3 日消息，Anthropic 计划投入 1 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 6.71 亿元人民币）培训 1 万名工程师，帮助企业把 AI 项目从构想真正推进到业务应用。
当地时间 2 日，Anthropic 宣布推出 Claude Frontier Academy（Claude 前沿学院）培训项目，瞄准企业 AI 落地过程中一个主要瓶颈：真正懂得如何把 AI 开发出来，并将其部署到企业实际业务中的人才仍然不足。
首批参加培训的工程师来自埃森哲、贝恩、凯捷、德勤、麦肯锡、摩根士丹利、诺和诺德和澳大利亚联邦银行。Anthropic 的目标是在 2027 年底前培养 1 万名前沿部署工程师。
按照安排，工程师首先会参加为期数天的线下培训，由 Anthropic 工程师和讲师授课，并通过模拟企业项目走完应用场景选择、安全审查和项目移交等环节。通过考核后，他们将进入 12 周的驻训阶段，回到各自所在机构负责一个真实的 Claude 项目。首批学员预计将在 2027 年初取得认证。
据《商业内幕》报道，这项计划也反映出，前沿部署工程师正成为 AI 行业越来越抢手的岗位。
前沿部署工程师直接与客户合作，根据客户现有的系统、数据和工作流程调整技术方案，不仅要参与确定开发什么，还要把新技术接入现有系统，并确保员工真正能够用起来。
2025 年 12 月，埃森哲成立 Anthropic Business Group，同时承诺为约 3 万名专业人员提供 Claude 培训，其中包括公司内部的“重塑部署工程师”。
上个月，埃森哲又与谷歌 Google Cloud 合作，派出 1000 名工程师，与大型客户一起部署 AI 智能体。
咨询公司过去就经常派团队进入客户机构解决问题。AI 普及后，这类工作需要更强的技术能力，工程师还得真正理解客户如何开展业务，前沿部署工程师因此开始发挥更大的作用。

Sean Parker, the Napster co-founder, has jumped back into the music industry, and he tells The Information that he’s playing by the rules this time. (Asking for forgiveness rather than permission didn’t work out so well last time around, he readily concedes.)

Two years ago, he joined an $80 million rescue of Stability AI, the image-generator startup that nearly collapsed after overspending and internal turmoil led to founder Emad Mostaque’s ouster. Now Parker and his longtime friend Prem Akkaraju, who became CEO, are taking the wraps off what they’ve been building.

The big idea, Parker says, is to turn Stability into the go-to AI toolmaker for music professionals. Toward that end, in late August, the company announced $76 million in funding from, among others, Sony, Warner, and Universal, which also licensed their catalogs for training as part of the deal. Stability has since released three new audio models and AI music-editing software. The AI can generate whole instrumental tracks or short snippets from text prompts. Parker says an upcoming update will let users hum a melody or beatbox a drum pattern to steer it.

fulltext: ﻿Meta now lets you connect Muse to your own hardware to put on your displays or a Raspberry Pi.

Meta now lets you make your own Muse gadgets that feature the company’s new AI agent with code that the company open sourced. The company suggests projects like loading Muse on a color E Ink display to show reminders, adding it to an HDMI stick so you can display Muse on a big screen, or putting Muse on a small touchscreen device to make what looks kind of like a DIY Muse Charm.

“Muse gadgets are open source devices you build yourself,” Meta says. “Program an off-the-shelf ESP32 board or set up a Raspberry Pi with our SDKs, then connect Muse to your displays, buttons, sensors, actuators, and whatever else you’ve got lying on your workbench.” However, Meta cautions that you should “Proceed at your own risk!”

The company is also giving away a Muse Home Link gadget that it created. With the Muse Home Link, you use community-built skills to have the AI agent “turn on a light, control your TV, send a document to a printer, and more, depending on your setup,” Meta says. It manufactured 5,000 of the gadgets, according to Meta Superintelligence Labs’ Nat Friedman, and you can claim a waitlist spot for the Muse Home Link now ahead of shipping sometime this month.

cards.title: Apple will limit Mac disk access as AI agents ‘substantially’ increase risk
cards.title_cn: 苹果将​​限制 Mac 磁盘访问，因为人工智能代理“大幅”增加了风险
cards.summary: 【Apple】Apple will add new limits for "full disk access" on Mac in response to risks posed by AI agents, as reported earlier by TechCrunch. In an update on Friday, Apple says it's rolling out new controls to…
fulltext: Mac apps will soon need ‘very explicit user action’ to gain full disk access, according to Apple.

Apple will add new limits for “full disk access” on Mac in response to risks posed by AI agents, as reported earlier by TechCrunch. In an update on Friday, Apple says it’s rolling out new controls to “ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so with very explicit user action.”

The change comes just weeks after Inc’s Jason Aten found that Meta’s Muse AI somehow knew the contents of his messages, despite not giving the chatbot explicit permission to access them on his iPhone or Mac. Meta spokesperson Andy Stone pushed back on this report, saying access to Messages is “entirely opt-in.” Stone added that you have to “enable both Full Disk Access and the Messages connector for Muse to be able to read your Messages content.”
Now Apple is addressing how developers use that sweeping access, saying:

Some developers are using Full Disk Access in ways that could put users at risk, exposing everything on their systems—including files, mail, messages, and even browsing history—without users’ full knowledge and understanding… As AI agents become increasingly capable and autonomous, the risks associated with this level of access will grow substantially.

Full disk access is a permission on macOS that gives an app access to a user’s entire system. Apple says the feature “largely sidesteps” privacy controls offered to users “to allow backup apps to function properly on Mac.” The company doesn’t say when it plans to roll out its update for full disk access. Apple didn’t immediately respond to The Verge’s request for comment.

cards.title: Audible has three new features to give you a deeper connection to your stories
cards.title_cn: Audible 拥有三项新功能，让您与故事有更深入的联系
cards.summary: 【Android Authority】Credit: Audible TL;DR Audible is rolling out three new AI-powered features: Character Guide, Interactive Story, and Visual Explorer. Character Guide helps listeners keep track of story characters, Int…
fulltext: Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission. Learn more.

After rolling out a rewards program earlier this year, Audible is back, giving listeners yet another reason to stick around. The company has a trio of new features that aim to make storytelling a little more immersive. However, these features won’t be available to everyone right out of the gate.

Audible has published a blog post, providing details on its upcoming features. These three new features are called Character Guide, Interactive Story, and Visual Explorer. Each powered by AI, these features take different approaches to deepen your connection to the story you’re enjoying.

If you’re having trouble keeping up with all of the characters in a story, Character Guide will help you keep track of the cast. This feature will show you who is talking in real time. On the player page, each character will have their own spoiler-free cards that also spotlight the performer behind the voice. You’ll also find the narrator’s headshots and bio here.

Character Guide is currently available for George Orwell’s 1984. It will also be available for Bram Stoker’s Dracula on October 1. Exoplanet from writer Benjamin Percy is also getting Character Guide on November 5. Audible says that down the road, users will be able to use this tool to ask questions about the production.

Interactive Story lets you throw yourself into the tale you’ve been listening to. The first Interactive Story will be for Bram Stoker’s Dracula, turning the narrative into an interactive conversation. Dracula’s servant, Renfield, will speak and assign the listener a role, goal, and stakes. As you respond, the character will listen and react in real time.
Audible says that the feature is designed to stay “faithful to the creator’s vision all the way through.” The next Interactive story will be Exoplanet, which will become available on November 5.

As the name suggests, Visual Explorer is designed to provide visual context to the story. During key moments, relevant imagery will be surfaced. It’s almost like turning your audiobook into a picture book. For example, while listening to The Cultural Tutor’s Grand Tour: The Story of Europe in Six Cities, you’ll see “imagery and bonus information about key landmarks, figures and places featured in six European cities.”

As mentioned earlier, not everyone will have access to these features initially. All three tools are being rolled out in a limited beta and will only come to users in the US and UK. The company does not say when it plans to expand availability.

cards.title: Chrome on Android’s password autofill could soon require a biometric test
cards.title_cn: Android 上的 Chrome 密码自动填充可能很快需要进行生物识别测试
cards.summary: 【Android Authority】TL;DR Google is testing biometric authentication before password autofill in Chrome for Android. The feature has returned in Chrome Canary after Google previously tested and pulled a similar implement…
fulltext: Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission. Learn more.

Google Chrome on Android does a lot of heavy lifting when it comes to passwords. With Google Password Manager, the browser lets you seamlessly add and save new passwords, complete with the option to use strong suggested options. And when you return to a website where you’ve previously saved your login credentials, Chrome can automatically fill them in for you. As convenient as that is, Google wants to add an additional step to that process.
Google is testing a new feature where Chrome on Android will require biometric authentication before it autofills passwords.

The development was first highlighted by browser sleuth Leopeva64 on X, who notes that this isn’t Google’s first rodeo with such a feature. The giant has been experimenting with the feature since September 2024, at the very least. It then made its way to Dev and Canary Chrome versions in August last year, only to be pulled before going stable. Now, Google appears to be giving the feature another shot.

The latest Chrome Canary build introduces a new flag called Biometric reauth for password filling, and it’s available to me after updating to the latest version 157.0.8083.0 Chrome Canary build via the Play Store.

Enabling the flag doesn’t do anything on my Pixel 8 for now, even after force-closing the app multiple times. That, however, is not the case for our source, as seen in the image above. For them, tapping a saved password under the “Use saved password?” prompt immediately triggers authentication. Chrome proceeds with autofilling the password only after the biometric check is completed.

The source also appears to be on an older version of Canary (version 157.0.8079.0). I rolled back to the older build, but I still couldn’t get the biometric speed bump to appear on my device, suggesting that the feature might not be tied solely to a specific Canary build. To try out the feature and check its availability for yourself, update Chrome Canary and search for chrome://flags. Type Biometric reauth for password filling in the search bar and toggle it to Enabled. Relaunch Chrome Canary as prompted and visit a website where you have a saved password.

The flag’s return does suggest that Google hasn’t entirely abandoned the authentication-before-autofill idea, and if it does materialize into a stable feature, it should give security-focused users more peace of mind, especially when handing their unlocked phone to someone else. That said, considering that the company has tested and pulled the feature before, there’s nothing stopping it from doing the same again.

Days after a journalist claimed that Meta’s Muse app on Mac read their private messages — a claim that Meta disputed — Apple announced that it’s introducing additional controls around a setting called “Full Disk Access” on macOS. The feature was designed to allow backups to function properly, but AI agents have now increased “the risks associated with this level of access,” Apple said.

Apple’s statement comes shortly after Inc. columnist Jason Aten reported that Muse knew the content of his private messages — even though he claimed to have not given the AI agent permission. The report raised questions about the level of security and trust users have in desktop-based AI, which can control things on their systems and read their files and messages.
The decision to limit the Mac feature also comes after a Wired report cited that a flaw in ChatGPT’s Mac app could have allowed hackers to access sensitive data.
AI agents that run on the desktop allow users to provide their respective apps with greater access to the files, messages, and other personal content on their computers by adjusting macOS settings.
In Muse’s case, the AI optionally allows users to enable Full Disk Access. This setting, Apple explains, gives an app permission to access files, mail, messages, and even browsing history.

“Some developers are using Full Disk Access in ways that could put users at risk, exposing everything on their systems…without users’ full knowledge and understanding,” Apple said in a new blog post aimed at developers.

The company says that, going forward, it will introduce new controls aimed at ensuring that users who “genuinely wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access” can do so only with “very explicit user action.”

“Addressing this is critical. As AI agents become increasingly capable and autonomous, the risks associated with this level of access will grow substantially. We are committed to ensuring users clearly understand these risks before granting such access, so they can make informed decisions about their own data and privacy,” Apple wrote.
Apple did not respond to TechCrunch’s inquiry about the feature change.

fulltext: Think of Dots as Codex, but for regular people.
It’s a tale as old as last week: OpenAI’s new agent platform, called Dots, is full of cute little guys who can do your bidding.
But unlike the ultra-approachable Meta Muse, Dots feel very much like using workplace software that happens to be able to order you a burrito — emphasis on work.

OpenAI announced Dots earlier this week. Like Muse, Dots have blobby, anthropomorphic avatars and customizable names. In the future, OpenAI says you’ll be able to have multiple Dots, but right now you get one. I named mine Dotty McDotface.

The interface looks similar to Muse’s; you chat with the agent in one window and follow its work in another as it clicks around on a virtual machine. But Dots are less personal shoppers, even though they can help you buy stuff. They’re more like coworkers: business software that can use other software. Your Dot’s virtual machine can access apps like Blender and GIMP right off the bat. You can also give it access to your own computer through the desktop ChatGPT app, and you can call your Dot if you need to work through things out loud. And OpenAI is offering Dots first to users on its highest-tier accounts, including the $100-per-month Pro account I expensed to test it. Muse and its buzzy competitor Instinct cost you nothing — at least now, and at least until Meta can get it off the ground and presumably start using it to serve you ads, etc. But OpenAI’s gated rollout says a lot about who the product is for, cute avatars notwithstanding.

I’ve been testing other AI agents with day-to-day personal tasks — yielding mixed results — and I was curious how OpenAI’s bot would compare. Despite its more enterprise-y vibes, OpenAI says Dots “can do nearly anything” with its cloud computer and access to apps, so I gave it a shot with some more pedestrian use cases.

To start, I had Dot try to schedule an installation appointment for a new internet service provider at my house (you hear that, Comcast? You’re on notice). It almost got there, and even found a $100 promotional discount in my email that I had mass deleted, but got stuck at a “human check.” Which is problematic for a bot. “This particular check needs a sustained mouse hold that my browser controls don’t support,” it said. “Please open my browser here and hold ‘Press & Hold’ until it completes, then tell me and I’ll continue with installation dates.” I obliged, but it felt a little bit like some teenagers outside of the convenience store asking me to buy them some wine coolers.

With my human ability to click and hold a button, Dot got all the way to the checkout screen, where it asked me to input my bank account details. Turns out there’s no slick Stripe integration like Muse has to save your credit card info and use a virtual card for checkout. And in any case, the new provider needed my bank account to get a $5 discount on my bill every month. Dot paused to let me enter the numbers into the virtual browser; I didn’t trust it well enough to punch in my checking account number and decided to just do it all myself on my own computer. Not exactly a spectacular start.

I gave Dot a few other personal tasks, and the results were mixed. It couldn’t find the option for a free tour and entry at a coworking space I’ve been meaning to try out, and instead offered to sign me up for a $35 day pass. I had Instinct’s agent, which I’ve also been testing, look for the trial option; it found it and set up an appointment within minutes. “Why did you miss this option?” I questioned Dot over the phone after the incident. “I jumped to the wrong conclusion,” it said. I hung up.

Later, I had it try to retrieve some information in my Ikea account about a hanging planter I bought. It reported that it was unable to log in to my Ikea account because it got stuck in a looping security check. Elsewhere on the internet, the neighborhood teriyaki spot wouldn’t allow Dot onto its ordering page. Something about Dot’s footprint seems to get it tripped up on security checks more often than Muse or Instinct; Dot offered a link to OpenAI’s page about websites blocking its cloud browser traffic as an explanation. Whatever the reason, it required more manual input and browser takeovers than other AI agents, possibly because it wasn’t purpose-built for ordering teriyaki or handling your Ikea returns.

I really saw Dot come into its element when I gave it access to something fully within my control: my personal website. It is embarrassingly outdated and I asked Dot to pull together a new, more streamlined design. It did, and when I sat down to type out some changes I want made for the next version, I thought, “To hell with it. I’ll just give it a call.” I hashed out the changes I wanted section by section over 10 minutes, walked away to do some dishes, and got a ping that the next iteration was ready for me to review. Not perfect, but better. Once again, AI proves most helpful when you give it a large dataset (me rambling for 10 minutes) it can turn into something useful. I carried out a few more rounds of iterations chatting with Dot in a browser window on my computer and using voice-to-text on the phone app as I walked around the house cleaning up Brio train tracks and stuffies.
Something about Dot’s footprint seems to get it tripped up on security checks more often than Muse or Instinct

Dot made a lot more sense once I gave it access to my computer. There, I gave it two tasks: Put together a handful of video files on my desktop featuring a TV hit I did into one clip sized properly for social media, and deploy the changes to my personal website that we had worked through in a prototype. I had to give it a shocking number of permissions, but it worked. I watched it click around the website backend and re-create the prototype block by block. I walked away from the computer and got updates on the ChatGPT app on my phone — the consolidated video clip was ready, which I reviewed while I drank a coffee. It was the most Silicon Valley I’ve ever felt in my life.

I absolutely could have figured out how to put all those clips together myself. In fact, I did the first time around, but it looked janky and was too big to upload on any social media website. Dot did a much better job and I had a clip to share within minutes. It handled the website update, too. The new design is basic, but it’s miles ahead of the complicated, out-of-date version I’d been rocking until yesterday. Gotta hand it to Dotty McDotface.

Dot makes a lot more sense when you think of it and use it as “Codex, but for regular people” — a cute little blob that can take care of some part of your business while you do other things. Where the more personal AI agents like Muse feel like glorified autofill and a universal online shopping cart, Dot seems like a harbinger of the future of work.

Or a future of work. Presumably, since you pay for it upfront, it won’t be subject to the kind of monetization pressure as Muse and Instinct eventually will, which makes sense for enterprise software. Nobody wants to be nagged by AI while they work. That is, assuming you do the kind of work that AI can help you with, and you trust OpenAI to do it. Big caveats!

It helped me out with some tasks that, if I’m being honest, I would have just not gotten around to doing. That’s pretty handy. But I don’t think it’s $100-a-month handy, at least in my line of work. I can see how it would be much more useful to someone like our friend Casey Newton, who’s in the thick of launching a new business.
And with some help logging into my Uber Eats account, it did actually order my teriyaki in the end.

cards.summary_cn: 【OpenAI】这是一个上周就有的故事：OpenAI 的新代理平台，名为 Dots，充满了可爱的小家伙，他们可以听从你的命令。但与超级平易近人的 Meta Muse 不同，Dots 感觉很像我们……
fulltext_cn: 将 Dots 视为 Codex，但适用于普通人。
这是一个上周就有的故事：OpenAI 的新代理平台，名为 Dots，充满了可爱的小家伙，他们可以听从你的命令。
但与超级平易近人的 Meta Muse 不同的是，Dots 感觉很像使用恰好能够为你点墨西哥卷饼的工作场所软件——强调工作。
OpenAI 本周早些时候发布了 Dots。与 Muse 一样，Dots 也有斑点、拟人化的头像和可自定义的名称。 OpenAI 表示，未来你将能够拥有多个 Dot，但现在你只有一个。我把我的名字命名为Dotty McDotface。

界面看起来与 Muse 类似；您可以在一个窗口中与代理聊天，并在代理在虚拟机上点击时在另一个窗口中跟踪其工作。但 Dots 并不是私人购物者，尽管他们可以帮助你买东西。他们更像是同事：可以使用其他软件的商业软件。您的 Dot 虚拟机可以立即访问 Blender 和 GIMP 等应用程序。您还可以通过桌面 ChatGPT 应用程序让它访问您自己的计算机，如果您需要大声解决问题，您可以致电您的 Dot。 OpenAI 首先向其最高级别账户的用户提供 Dots，其中包括我用于测试的每月 100 美元的 Pro 账户。 Muse 及其热门竞争对手 Instinct 不会让你花费任何成本——至少现在是这样，至少在 Meta 能够将其付诸实践并可能开始使用它为你提供广告等之前。但 OpenAI 的封闭式推出充分说明了该产品的适用人群，尽管有可爱的化身。
我一直在用日常个人任务测试其他人工智能代理，结果好坏参半，我很好奇 OpenAI 的机器人会如何比较。尽管 OpenAI 更具企业风格，但 OpenAI 表示 Dots 可以通过其云计算机和应用程序访问“几乎可以做任何事情”，因此我尝试了一些更普通的用例。

首先，我让 Dot 尝试为我家的新互联网服务提供商安排安装预约（康卡斯特，你听到了吗？你注意到了）。差点就到了，甚至在我的电子邮件中发现了 100 美元的促销折扣，我已将其批量删除，但陷入了“人工检查”。这对于机器人来说是有问题的。 “这项特殊检查需要持续按住鼠标，但我的浏览器控件不支持，”它说。 “请在此处打开我的浏览器并按住‘按住’直到完成，然后告诉我，我将继续安装日期。”我答应了，但感觉有点像便利店外的一些青少年要求我给他们买一些酒柜。

凭借我点击并按住按钮的人类能力，Dot 一直到达结帐屏幕，它要求我输入我的银行帐户详细信息。事实证明，没有像 Muse 那样灵活的 Stripe 集成来保存您的信用卡信息并使用虚拟卡进行结帐。无论如何，新提供商需要我的银行帐户才能每月为我的账单提供 5 美元的折扣。点停下来让我在虚拟浏览器中输入数字；我不太信任它，无法输入我的支票帐号，因此决定自己在自己的计算机上完成这一切。不完全是一个壮观的开始。
我给了多特一些其他的个人任务，结果好坏参半。它找不到免费参观和进入我一直想尝试的联合办公空间的选项，而是为我提供了 35 美元的一日通行证。我有 Instinct 的代理，我也一直在测试它，寻找试用选项；它找到了它并在几分钟内安排了约会。 “为什么你错过了这个选项？”事件发生后我通过电话询问了多特。 “我得出了错误的结论，”它说。我挂断了电话。

后来，我让它尝试在我的宜家帐户中检索有关我购买的悬挂花盆的一些信息。据报道，它无法登录我的宜家帐户，因为它陷入了循环安全检查。在互联网的其他地方，附近的照烧店不允许 Dot 进入其订购页面。 Dot 的足迹似乎比 Muse 或 Instinct 更容易在安全检查中被绊倒； Dot 提供了 OpenAI 页面上有关阻止其云浏览器流量的网站的链接作为解释。不管是什么原因，它比其他人工智能代理需要更多的手动输入和浏览器接管，可能是因为它不是专门为订购照烧或处理宜家退货而设计的。

当我让 Dot 访问完全在我控制范围内的东西时，我真的看到了它的元素：我的个人网站。它已经过时了，令人尴尬，我要求 Dot 整合一个新的、更精简的设计。确实如此，当我坐下来输入我想要对下一个版本进行的一些更改时，我想，“见鬼去吧。我只是给它打电话。”我用了 10 分钟的时间逐节讨论了我想要的更改，然后走开去做一些菜，并得到一个通知，表明下一个迭代已准备好供我审查。不完美，但更好。再一次证明，当你给人工智能一个大数据集（我闲聊了 10 分钟）时，它可以变成有用的东西，它是最有帮助的。当我在房子里走来走去清理 Brio 火车轨道和玩具时，我又进行了几轮迭代，在计算机上的浏览器窗口中与 Dot 聊天，并在手机应用程序上使用语音转文本。
Dot 的足迹似乎比 Muse 或 Instinct 更容易在安全检查中被绊倒

当我允许 Dot 访问我的计算机后，它就变得更有意义了。在那里，我给了它两项任务：将我桌面上的一些视频文件放在一起，其中包含我制作的一个电视热门视频，将其制作成一个大小适合社交媒体的剪辑，并将我们在原型中完成的更改部署到我的个人网站。我不得不授予它数量惊人的权限，但它确实有效。我看着它在网站后端点击并逐块重新创建原型。我离开电脑，在手机上的 ChatGPT 应用程序上获取更新 - 合并的视频剪辑已准备就绪，我一边喝咖啡一边查看。这是我一生中感受到的最硅谷的感觉。
我绝对可以自己想出如何将所有这些剪辑放在一起。事实上，我第一次这样做了，但它看起来很糟糕，而且太大，无法上传到任何社交媒体网站上。点做得更好，我在几分钟内就有了一个可以分享的剪辑。它还处理了网站更新。新的设计很基本，但它比我昨天才使用的复杂、过时的版本领先了很多。必须把它交给多蒂·麦克多特法斯。
当你将 Dot 视为“Codex，但对于普通人来说”时，它就更有意义了——一个可爱的小斑点，可以在你做其他事情的同时照顾你的某些业务。像 Muse 这样更加个性化的人工智能代理感觉像是美化的自动填充和通用在线购物车，而 Dot 似乎是未来工作的预兆。
或者未来的工作。据推测，由于您预先付费，因此它不会像 Muse 和 Instinct 最终那样受到货币化压力，这对于企业软件来说是有意义的。没有人愿意在工作时被人工智能打扰。也就是说，假设您所做的工作是 AI 可以帮助您完成的，并且您信任 OpenAI 可以做到这一点。大警告！
它帮助我完成了一些任务，老实说，我根本没有时间去做这些任务。这非常方便。但我认为每月 100 美元不太方便，至少在我的工作中是这样。我可以想象，对于像我们的朋友凯西·牛顿这样正忙于开展新业务的人来说，这会更加有用。
在登录我的 Uber Eats 优食账户的帮助下，它最终确实点了我的照烧。
